description: Composite figure mixing three SEM micrographs with one EDX elemental-mapping panel, all for steel S4. (a) SEM, TA 1250 °C / TB 350 °C: coarse bainitic sheaf (lamellar) structure with sparse bright elongated particles labelled "TiMoC precipitates"; 10 µm scale bar. (b) SEM, TA 1150 °C / TB 350 °C: large featureless matrix areas with bright precipitates strung out along near-horizontal rows, and an arrow labelling a dark angular particle "AlN"; 10 µm scale bar. (c) SEM, TA 1150 °C / TB 320 °C: markedly finer, denser sheaf/needle morphology, also labelled "TiMoC precipitates"; 10 µm scale bar. (d) EDX mapping of (c), four false-colour maps each with a 10 µm scale bar: Fe Kα1 (blue), C Kα1,2 (orange), Ti Kα1 (red), Mo Lα1 (yellow). Needle-shaped precipitates are dark (depleted) in the Fe map and bright (enriched) in the C, Ti and Mo maps, so the particles imaged in (c) are Ti–Mo carbides. The group links morphology (a–c) to chemistry (d), evidencing TiMoC precipitates in the bainitic matrix and local Fe depletion inside them.
measured_quantities: EDX element maps: Fe Kα1, C Kα1,2, Ti Kα1, Mo Lα1

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an SEM micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar showing a coarse bainitic sheaf structure with sparse bright elongated particles annotated 'TiMoC precipitates'.
Panel (b) shows a largely featureless matrix with bright precipitates aligned along near-horizontal bands, and an arrow labelling a dark angular particle as 'AlN'.
Panel (c) shows a distinctly finer and denser sheaf/needle morphology than (a) or (b), annotated 'TiMoC precipitates'.
Panel (d) contains four EDX maps labelled Fe Kα1, C Kα1,2, Ti Kα1 and Mo Lα1, each with its own 10 µm scale bar; no colour-scale legend or concentration scale is shown.
In panel (d) the needle-shaped regions that are dark (depleted) in the Fe Kα1 map are bright (enriched) in the Ti Kα1 and Mo Lα1 maps, and correspond to the precipitates imaged in (c).
The caption states the panel conditions: (a) SEM for S4, TA 1250 °C, TB 350 °C; (b) SEM for S4, TA 1150 °C, TB 350 °C; (c) SEM for S4, TA 1150 °C, TB 320 °C; (d) EDX mapping of (c).
The citation asserts that a depletion of Fe was detected within the complex carbides in the EDX mapping, confirming their composition (Fig. 10 (d)).

The citation asserts that the longitudinal alignment of the TiMoC precipitates indicates formation during cooling after casting followed by deformation during hot forming, with negligible secondary precipitation (Fig. 10 (a), (b), (c)).
The citation asserts that the Ti–Mo–C complex carbides lack micro-defects within the microstructure (Fig. 10 (a), (b), (c)).
The citation attributes the suppressed bainite transformation progress in S4 to impingement of bainite sheaves caused by an increased number of phase boundaries, referring to Fig. 10.

The caption labels the austempering temperature of panel (c) without a subscript ('T: 320 °C'), whereas panels (a) and (b) use TB; the condition is presumably TB 320 °C but the printed caption is ambiguous.

subfigures.description: SEM micrograph of S4 (TA 1250 °C, TB 350 °C) showing a coarse bainitic sheaf/lamellar matrix with bright elongated precipitates labelled 'TiMoC precipitates'; 10 µm scale bar at bottom right.

SEM micrograph of S4 (TA 1150 °C, TB 350 °C) showing broad featureless matrix regions with bright elongated precipitates aligned in near-horizontal rows, top-left label 'TiMoC precipitates', and an arrow pointing to a dark angular particle labelled 'AlN'; 10 µm scale bar.
SEM micrograph of S4 (TA 1150 °C, TB 320 °C) showing a much finer, denser sheaf/needle bainitic structure with the label 'TiMoC precipitates'; 10 µm scale bar.

Four side-by-side EDX elemental maps of the area in (c): Fe Kα1 (blue, showing dark depleted regions), C Kα1,2 (orange), Ti Kα1 (red) and Mo Lα1 (yellow), with the Ti/Mo/C maps bright in the same needle-shaped regions that are dark in Fe; each map has a 10 µm scale bar labelled '10µm'.
